es: Redactar los resultados de una encuesta escolar con conectores formales, cifras, una fuente y afirmaciones matizadas.

vocabulary.es: a la inversa, por el contrario

teaching.en: Furthermore, the percentage of students who sleep under seven hours rises in the final year, reaching seventy percent in some classes.
teaching.es: Además, el porcentaje de estudiantes que duerme menos de siete horas sube en el último curso, hasta llegar al setenta por ciento en algunas clases.
teaching.explanationEs: Furthermore añade un dato en la misma línea y es más formal que and also; percentage es el porcentaje (sin the delante de la cifra).
segments: Furthermore, the percentage of students who sleep under seven hours rises
in the final year, reaching seventy percent in some classes.
teaching.audioText: Furthermore, the percentage of students who sleep under seven hours rises in the final year, reaching seventy percent in some classes.

teaching.en: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a very small group.
teaching.es: Solo una minoría de los encuestados usa el móvil después de medianoche; sin embargo, son los que dicen dormir peor, si bien en un grupo muy pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless contrasta con lo anterior: antes lleva punto y coma, y después, coma. Albeit introduce una salvedad (= although it is).
segments: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; nevertheless,
they report the worst sleep, albeit in a very small group.
teaching.audioText: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a very small group.

teaching.en: Most respondents said that they feel tired in the morning; therefore, the school may wish to review the timetable.
teaching.es: La mayoría de los encuestados dijo que se siente cansada por la mañana; por tanto, el colegio podría querer revisar el horario.
teaching.explanationEs: Therefore introduce la consecuencia. Lleva punto y coma o punto delante, no una simple coma.
segments: Most respondents said that they feel tired in the morning;
therefore, the school may wish to review the timetable.
teaching.audioText: Most respondents said that they feel tired in the morning; therefore, the school may wish to review the timetable.

teaching.en: These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little, in terms of both hours and quality.
teaching.es: Estos resultados son coherentes con la encuesta nacional, que afirmó que los adolescentes duermen poco, tanto en horas como en calidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Consistent with integra una fuente externa; stated introduce lo que dijo esa fuente (pasado); in terms of + sustantivo delimita el aspecto.
segments: These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that
teenagers sleep too little, in terms of both hours and quality.
teaching.audioText: These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little, in terms of both hours and quality.

teaching.en: Notably, the biggest rise was among students in their final year; conversely, the youngest students reported no change at all.
teaching.es: En particular, el mayor aumento se dio entre los estudiantes del último curso; a la inversa, los más jóvenes no notificaron ningún cambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Notably destaca un dato concreto dentro de los resultados; conversely presenta el caso opuesto.
segments: Notably, the biggest rise was among students in their final
year; conversely, the youngest students reported no change at all.
teaching.audioText: Notably, the biggest rise was among students in their final year; conversely, the youngest students reported no change at all.

teaching.en: All year groups showed the same pattern, with the exception of the first year, where the percentage of tired students fell slightly.
teaching.es: Todos los cursos mostraron el mismo patrón, con la excepción del primero, donde el porcentaje de estudiantes cansados bajó ligeramente.
teaching.explanationEs: With the exception of + sustantivo señala el único caso que no sigue la regla.
segments: All year groups showed the same pattern, with the exception of
the first year, where the percentage of tired students fell slightly.
teaching.audioText: All year groups showed the same pattern, with the exception of the first year, where the percentage of tired students fell slightly.

prompt.es: Elige la frase formal que añade el segundo dato en el apartado de resultados.

choices.text: Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, reaching 70 percent.
Anyway, it's higher in the final year, like 70 percent or so.
In conclusion, the percentage is higher in the final year, reaching 70 percent.

feedback.es: Furthermore suma un dato en un registro formal; anyway es coloquial e in conclusion cierra el texto en lugar de añadir información.

hint.es: Busca el conector formal que suma un dato, no el que concluye ni el coloquial.

origin.text: Data for the results section: 60 percent of the respondents sleep under eight hours. In the final year the figure is 70 percent. The writer wants a formal connector that adds the second fact to the first one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Solo una minoría usa el móvil después de medianoche; sin embargo, duerme peor.»

feedback.es: Nevertheless contrasta dos datos: pocos usan el móvil, pero ese grupo duerme peor. Lleva punto y coma delante y coma detrás.

hint.es: Es el conector formal que significa «sin embargo» y va tras punto y coma.

origin.text: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; ___, they report the worst sleep of the whole sample.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por tanto, el colegio podría plantearse un inicio más tardío.»

answer.text: Therefore the school may wish to consider a later start

feedback.es: Therefore introduce la consecuencia del dato anterior; may wish to es una forma cortés y prudente de recomendar.

hint.es: Empieza por el conector que introduce la consecuencia.

prompt.es: Escucha el párrafo modelo y elige qué relación establece «nevertheless».

choices.text: It adds one more reason why students sleep badly.
It contrasts students who sleep well with their tiredness.
It draws a consequence from the previous figure.

feedback.es: Nevertheless une dos ideas que chocan: duermen bien y aun así se sienten cansados.

origin.audio: Listen to this model paragraph. The survey found that forty percent of respondents use a phone after midnight. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year. Only a minority of students sleep well; nevertheless, they still report feeling tired. It appears that exams may play a role, which matches what the national survey found. Therefore, the school may wish to review its timetable.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le reprocha principalmente la profesora a la estudiante.

choices.text: That her numbers are wrong and come from no named survey.
That she uses too many formal connectors in every single sentence.
That her writing does not show clearly how her ideas connect.

feedback.es: La profesora critica que la estudiante usa siempre and y but, de modo que no se ve cómo se relacionan las ideas.

origin.audio: Your results section has good numbers, but the writing needs work. First, you use and and but for everything, so the reader cannot see how your ideas connect. A formal report would say furthermore to add a fact, nevertheless to contrast, and therefore to show a consequence. Second, you wrote that the national survey agrees with you, but you never named it, so I cannot check it. Finally, you say that phones cause tiredness. Your data show only a link, so it would be safer to say that it appears that phones may play a role.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué habría que cambiar en la frase sobre los móviles.

choices.text: The claim of a cause should become a cautious statement about a link.
The figure for phones should be replaced with the national one instead.
The whole sentence should be moved to the method section of the report.

feedback.es: Los datos solo muestran un vínculo: la profesora propone sustituir la causa afirmada por it appears that… may play a role.

origin.text: The figures are similar in every year group. ___, the highest percentage is found in the final year, where it reaches seventy percent.

prompt.es: Escribe la sección de resultados con tres conectores, una fuente y dos matices.

answer.text: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Conversely, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep fewer than eight hours. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep, albeit on a small sample. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.
accepted: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Conversely, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep fewer than eight hours. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep, albeit on a small sample. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.

According to the survey of 150 students, 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours, and the figure rises to 70 percent in the final year. Moreover, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep so little. A minority of respondents, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; however, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a small group. There is some evidence that phones may affect sleep, but the data do not show that they are the cause. The findings are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers do not sleep enough. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a later start. Notably, the figure is highest in the final year, and further research would be useful.

The survey of 150 students found that 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours. In addition, the percentage rises to 70 percent in the final year, whereas it is 45 percent in the first year. A minority, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; even so, these students report the worst sleep. It seems that late phone use may play a role, although the survey cannot prove it. According to the national survey, teenagers sleep too little, so the results are consistent with earlier research. As a result, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the final year shows the highest figure, and more evidence would be welcome.

feedback.es: La sección combina cifras, tres conectores formales, una fuente y al menos dos afirmaciones matizadas (it appears that, may, tend to).

origin.text: Encuesta escolar sobre el sueño (150 estudiantes): el 60 % duerme menos de ocho horas; en último curso, el 70 %; en primer curso, el 45 %; el 18 % usa el móvil después de medianoche y duerme peor. La encuesta nacional afirma que los adolescentes duermen poco. Escribe unas 125 a 200 palabras: tres conectores formales (furthermore, nevertheless, therefore…), la fuente y dos afirmaciones matizadas.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que integra la fuente nacional con prudencia.

choices.text: Our figure of 60 percent proves the national report, which is obviously right about teenagers everywhere.
Our figure of 60 percent is consistent with the national report, which stated that 55 percent sleep too little.
Our figure of 60 percent contradicts the national report, although the two numbers are in fact very close.

feedback.es: Consistent with cita la fuente sin exagerar; proves y contradicts dicen más o algo distinto de lo que muestran las dos cifras.

origin.text: You must refer to a national report that found that 55 percent of teenagers sleep under eight hours. Your own school survey found 60 percent. The two figures are close, and your sample is much smaller than theirs.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué prefiere Mia la segunda versión de la frase.

choices.text: Because it is shorter and easier to read aloud.
Because it includes figures that the first one lacks.
Because it matches what the survey actually shows.

feedback.es: Mia prefiere la segunda porque refleja un vínculo, no una causa, y un informe no debe afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.audio: Mia is reading out two versions of a sentence. The first says that phones are the reason why students sleep badly. The second says that it appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep. She prefers the second one, because the survey shows a link and not a cause, and a good report should never claim more than the data allow.

prompt.es: Completa: «Solo una minoría de los encuestados usa el móvil después de medianoche.»

feedback.es: Minority significa menos de la mitad; combina con only para dejar claro que el grupo es pequeño.
